item.title: docs: ADR 0011 — contribution model, feature intake, legacy archive (no required approval)
item.body:
**Problem.** A parallel session had written a second ADR 0010 (contribution model) on a branch of `francoisgn/ios-app_SwiftHFR` that was never merged.

**What changed**
- **ADR 0011** (renumbered), with only what ADR 0010 does not already decide:
  - branches in `ezzz/HFRnow` for maintainers, forks for everyone else;
  - how an idea becomes code (lot claim in LOTS.md and lot spec, migration loop of AGENTS.md §5);
  - the Objective-C archive at the production switch.
- **No human approval required**: maintainer decision. In a team of three it would stall the work. The safeguards are the 9 required checks, resolved conversations and the second-model review. The ADR says when to revisit: if write access goes beyond ezzz, francoisgn and moust4ki.
- Removes the "approval once ADR 0011 is accepted" mentions from CONTRIBUTING, the README and both diagrams (regenerated).

**Checks**: markdownlint, 0 errors. Docs only.

Walkthrough
The pull request adds proposed ADR 0011 on contribution roles, review requirements, feature intake, and the planned legacy archive. It also adds the ADR to the index. **Changes: Contribution model and feature intake** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**ADR proposal and index**
`docs/adr/0011-contribution-model-and-feature-intake.md`, `docs/adr/README.md`|The proposed ADR describes contribution and review rules, a staged feature-intake process, and plans for the legacy archive and default branch. The index lists ADR 0011 as proposed.| Priority: Low **Estimated code review effort:** 2 (Simple) | ~10 minutes **Change:** Other **Possibly related PRs** - [ezzz/HFRnow#9](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/pull/9): Adds the same ADR and index entry; this pull request replaces it and excludes its ruleset change. - [ezzz/HFRnow#8](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/pull/8): Establishes the `dev-swift` integration branch, which ADR 0011 identifies as the contribution target.
Merge Risk: Low · up to 0d583
The documentation-only change remains low risk, but clarify the lot workflow and approval bypass before accepting the ADR.
Security architecture risk: Low · up to 0d583
The proposal does not change merge permissions, workflow execution, or deployment behavior. Existing permission to merge without independent approval remains, so adopting the policy must be distinguished from enforcing it. The archive and default-branch switch are explicitly deferred. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.
Security review details
**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The supported merge-control exposure is contributor-controlled code entering dev-swift through existing merge privileges, rather than new authority granted to an external fork author. The inspected ruleset is branch-scoped, and the proposal neither changes repository membership nor grants deployment credentials. **Security Findings and Attack Paths** - _observed_ — The retained finding concerns independent-review enforcement. ADR 0011 states that write collaborators can self-merge with green checks; the repository ruleset requires zero approvals and includes an always-bypass RepositoryRole actor 5. Both configuration conditions predate this PR. The actor's role mapping and the live GitHub configuration were not established. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — The three routed workflows use pull_request triggers and credential-nonpersisting checkouts. CI declares contents: read and executes repository tests and scripts. CodeQL jobs request security-events: write, and dependency review requests pull-requests: write. Their complete workflow files contain no explicit repository-secret references, but requested scopes alone do not establish effective fork-token permissions or runner-side secret isolation. - _observed_ — Existing governance assigns repository-wide security settings to the owner because they also affect legacy master. ADR 0011 requires owner agreement and defers enforcement, so accepting documentation and applying the live control remain distinct administrative states. **Hardening Proposals** - _proposed_ — At adoption, verify the effective live approval requirement and intended bypass exceptions before treating independent review as enforced. In the separate production-switch procedure, define ownership, ordered checkpoints, protected archive identity, and repeatable recovery for interrupted branch and automation changes.

+# 0011 — Contribution model, feature intake and legacy archive
+
+**Status:** Proposed — 2026-10-27 (maintainer; needs the agreement of ezzz, owner of the repository). Hosting itself is [ADR 0010](0010-hosting-on-ezzz-hfrnow-dev-swift.md).
+
+## Context
+- SwiftHFR lives on `ezzz/HFRnow:dev-swift` ([ADR 0010](0010-hosting-on-ezzz-hfrnow-dev-swift.md)). `master` is the shipped Objective-C app with its `HFRswift/` SwiftUI layer.
+- New contributors arrive with different practices. The first one (Bybifok, `moust4ki`) builds UI-first with an agent, without specs, tests or adversarial review, and opened PRs #3–#6 on `master`. They compiled, yet dropped user settings, broke `[code]` fonts and replaced a just-finished navigation.
+- `write` collaborators (`francoisgn`, `moust4ki`) can merge their own PR on green CI alone.
+- Q-1 is decided (2026-10-26): SwiftHFR ships as an update of the existing App Store app `hfrplus.red.super`, from this repository.
+- PRs from forks run `pull_request` workflows **without secrets** and with a read-only token.
+
+## Decision
+
+### 1. Who works where
+| Role | Where they push | PR target |
+|---|---|---|
+| Maintainers (ezzz, francoisgn) and their agent sessions | branches in `ezzz/HFRnow` (`lot/…`, `fix/…`, `feat/…`, `chore/…`, `docs/…`, `claude/…`) | `dev-swift` |
+| Everyone else, including invited contributors | their own fork, whatever their role | `dev-swift` |
+
+- Contributing never requires write access. The recommended role for an invited contributor is **Triage** (labels, issues).
+- Every PR on `dev-swift` needs **one approving review by someone other than its author**, on top of the checks of ADR 0005. With write access, green CI alone would allow self-merges.
+- PRs to `master` that change SwiftHFR scope are redirected to `dev-swift`.
+- Every required check passes **without secrets** (fork PRs). `pull_request_target` with a checkout of PR code is forbidden.
+
+### 2. Feature intake
+An idea, a prototype or a mock-up becomes code in this order: feature issue → spec `docs/features/FEAT-XXX.md` (what and why, screens and states, HFR facts with their source, edge cases, engine lots needed, legacy settings kept) → engine lots in `docs/LOTS.md` when `HFRKit` lacks a capability → app PRs, one feature slice each, meeting AGENTS.md §9.

+- Prototype code is a reference, like the legacy app ([ADR 0004](0004-legacy-app-as-oracle.md)), not code to merge as is.

**Security Misconfiguration** **Reachability:** Internal **Exploitability:** Difficult **CWE:** [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html) [View Security blast radius](https://app.coderabbit.ai/change-stack/ezzz/HFRnow/pull/10/blast-radius?scope=ghh_OusAJGA4HG8ljoOV0wJvVx8NmnZIjc2DdjmxOu0xZWA&toCommitId=0d5838049813e12c6de3f36b124ed853f033f4c4&reviewRunId=33c1cabe-acca-4b80-aed3-50b69a3afaf7&securityFinding=2a6fc9790cc87509dc7d8f33) **The ADR's approval guarantee does not account for the ruleset's bypass actor.** Line 40 says a maintainer's PR waits for another approval once the count is 1. The current `.github/rulesets/dev-swift.json` grants actor `5` (`RepositoryRole`, `bypass_mode: "always"`). A bypass actor skips the pull request rule, including its approval requirement. If actor `5` is the repository admin role, an admin can merge without a second review once the count is raised. Changing the count alone does not give the guarantee that the ADR states. The count is `0` today, so the gap applies only after the count changes. Confirm in the repository settings what actor `5` maps to. Do not change the ruleset without the operator's prior confirmation, as `AGENTS.md` requires for repository settings. Record the decision in the ADR.
Document the bypass in ADR 0011

+**Status:** Proposed — 2026-10-27 (maintainer; needs the agreement of ezzz, owner of the repository). Hosting itself is [ADR 0010](0010-hosting-on-ezzz-hfrnow-dev-swift.md).
+
+## Context
+- SwiftHFR lives on `ezzz/HFRnow:dev-swift` ([ADR 0010](0010-hosting-on-ezzz-hfrnow-dev-swift.md)). `master` is the shipped Objective-C app with its `HFRswift/` SwiftUI layer.
+- New contributors arrive with different practices. The first one (Bybifok, `moust4ki`) builds UI-first with an agent, without specs, tests or adversarial review, and opened PRs #3–#6 on `master`. They compiled, yet dropped user settings, broke `[code]` fonts and replaced a just-finished navigation.
+- `write` collaborators (`francoisgn`, `moust4ki`) can merge their own PR on green CI alone.
+- Q-1 is decided (2026-10-26): SwiftHFR ships as an update of the existing App Store app `hfrplus.red.super`, from this repository.
+- PRs from forks run `pull_request` workflows **without secrets** and with a read-only token.
+
+## Decision
+
+### 1. Who works where
+| Role | Where they push | PR target |
+|---|---|---|
+| Maintainers (ezzz, francoisgn) and their agent sessions | branches in `ezzz/HFRnow` (`lot/…`, `fix/…`, `feat/…`, `chore/…`, `docs/…`, `claude/…`) | `dev-swift` |
+| Everyone else, including invited contributors | their own fork, whatever their role | `dev-swift` |
+
+- Contributing never requires write access. The recommended role for an invited contributor is **Triage** (labels, issues).
+- Every PR on `dev-swift` needs **one approving review by someone other than its author**, on top of the checks of ADR 0005. With write access, green CI alone would allow self-merges.
+- PRs to `master` that change SwiftHFR scope are redirected to `dev-swift`.
+- Every required check passes **without secrets** (fork PRs). `pull_request_target` with a checkout of PR code is forbidden.
+
+### 2. Feature intake
+An idea, a prototype or a mock-up becomes code in this order: feature issue → spec `docs/features/FEAT-XXX.md` (what and why, screens and states, HFR facts with their source, edge cases, engine lots needed, legacy settings kept) → engine lots in `docs/LOTS.md` when `HFRKit` lacks a capability → app PRs, one feature slice each, meeting AGENTS.md §9.

+- Prototype code is a reference, like the legacy app ([ADR 0004](0004-legacy-app-as-oracle.md)), not code to merge as is.
+- A feature that reads or writes something new on the forum first gets its facts into `docs/HFR-PROTOCOL.md`, with evidence (AGENTS.md §3).
+- The author of an idea is credited in the spec, in the PR that implements it and in `CREDITS.md`, whoever writes the code.
+
+### 3. Legacy Objective-C archive
+At the production switch (separate ADR):
+- tag `legacy/objc-final` on the last `master` commit that shipped the Objective-C app, and branch `archive/objc` from it (protected, read-only);
+- `dev-swift` becomes the default branch content; CI and default-branch automation move with it.
+The archive stays the functional blueprint and the oracle of [ADR 0004](0004-legacy-app-as-oracle.md). Until then, oracle exports name the legacy commit they ran on.
+
+## Consequences
+- One integration branch, one process: the rules in `AGENTS.md` apply to every contributor.
+- The shipped app and SwiftHFR never share a PR; nothing in SwiftHFR work can break a TestFlight build.
+- The required review is applied in `.github/rulesets/dev-swift.json` (`required_approving_review_count: 1`) once this ADR is accepted. A maintainer's PR then waits for someone else's approval; lower the count only if every write member is a maintainer.
